main_text.p: Christianæ. Neque enim hoc volunta-rias, & in utrumque contrarium ver-sas hominū actiones, tollit: ut tollit fa-tū Stoicū violentum. Quomodo enim, nisi contra seipsum, ibidem agnosce-ret: ut creationem; ita regenerationem hominis per fidem, esse divinæ gratiæ? Et quomodo creatio tolleret liberū arbitrium; quod nondum erat? Utrobique, & ante & post regenerationem, fatemur id; quod laudat idem alibi, ut à Mose sumtum, Platonis: Culpa est eligentis hominis; nulla Dei. Et: Fatum hoc esse immutabile: ut recta-eligentibus, digna præmia; & similiter contraria-eligentibus, digna sint pœnæ. At inde tamen, ut non efficitur, fa-tum id esse Stoicum: ita nec, nos, sine auxilio gratiaque Dei singulari, recta posse efficere. quia, quæ recta sunt, teste eodem, (Paraenesi ad Græcos) ignora-mus.
Porrò, ita quoque Irenæus, ex seipso,Irenæus explicandus est. Etsi enim liberum videtur statuere arbitrium, cùm alibi, tum quando inquit lib. 4. adversus hæ-reses.

page.notes: The left edge of the scan shows cut-off fragments of the neighbouring page (outer margin of the left page); left out. Page number printed as "6ı." (the number 61, with an unusual 'ı'). The right-margin marginal note "Irenæus" is read as printed. The catchword "res." is read as "res.". No running head or signature visible. The final line "adversus hæ-reses" is partly cut off at the bottom of the printed line and the line end is read as "hæ-" and "res"; the completion "reses" is taken from the catchword and should be checked against the scan.
